messages:
mike: heads-up — saw a pronounced tail latency spike (~200ms P99 -> 600ms) starting at 09:12 while running the grpc streaming perf run. looks correlated with bursty small-chunk streams to the host.
anya: repro steps? is this on canary or prod? :thinking_face:
mike: canary pool. trace: https://internal-traces/trace/4487654321 — you can see long pause inside host request parsing; profiler shows threads queued on tokenizer pool mutex.
sasha: hmm tokenizer-pool starvation again? we changed pool size to 4 last month for mem pressure.
david: I dug into the flamegraph — the blocked time is in tokenize_one_request -> acquire_tokenizer -> wait on workqueue. concurrent requests spike and kernels switched to mini-batch path (mini-batch kernel) at the same time.
anya: so two things aligned: bursty grpc small writes (many small frames) + kernel selector flipped to minibatch mode -> more concurrency trying to use limited tokenizer workers.
mike: exactly. also saw writev coalesce was disabled for that proxy (canary flags), so extra syscall overhead made parsing slower, aggravating queueing.
infra-bot: deploy canary/rls-2026-03-20 finished — 09:05 UTC
sasha: probable fix options:
- bump tokenizer pool to 8 for canary and observe (low risk)
- re-enable writev coalesce on proxy path
- add a quick gating heuristic in kernel selector to avoid switching to mini-batch under <X req/s small-frame pattern
- add per-request parse timeout metric to catch early next time
anya: I can flip writev coalesce on the canary proxy now, then bump pool if it persists. who wants kernel-selector change?
david: I'll take the kernel selector heuristic. quick patch: if avg_frame_size < 256 and incoming qps > 400 -> prefer slim single-token kernel. should be small change.
mike: thanks. can we also add an alert for tokenizer queue depth > 3 sustained? that would've caught this earlier.
anya: added to backlog and created a lightweight alert for queue depth > 3 for 1m. assigning to sasha for immediate pool bump.
sasha: rolling pool size from 4->8 on canary now. will report metrics in 5m. :thumbsup:
mike: if that doesn't fix P99 I'll cut the kernel selector patch for a canary roll tomorrow. documented short postmortem here: https://docs/internal/host-tailspike-2026-03-20
david: posted a short profiler snippet in the trace comments with call stacks and suggested patch link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/hosts/commit/abcdef
mike: great work team. follow-ups: sasha confirm pool bump results; david open PR for selector heuristic; anya validate that writev coalesce change didn't regress memory.
anya: will do. closing loop in 10m with metrics.
